answer: A physical unclonable function protocol curbs Sybil attacks by querying microscopic silicon variations on each device. Verifiers issue challenge vectors at the dawn of each epoch, proving costless duplication is a fable. Because unique gate delays prevent emulation, an adversary cannot forge responses without incurring the verifiable cost of procuring discrete microchips per agent. However, ambient thermal drift causes read instability, occasionally rejecting authentic nodes.
